title: Etale cohomology of a strictly henselian local scheme vanishes in positive degrees
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the global sections functor $\Gamma(S,-):\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\textit{Ab}$ on abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is exact, and $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal F\in\Ab(S_{\Et})$ and every $p\ge1$ (etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian, line 8207), the final assertion and the last sentence of its proof ('the higher derived functors of an exact functor are zero'); the exactness via Gamma(S, F) = F_sbar is [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk]

proof.text: *A geometric point over the closed point.* Let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $R$, $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ its residue field and $s\in S$ the closed point $\mathfrak m$, so $\kappa(s)=\kappa$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Choose an algebraic closure $\iota:\kappa\to\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] (it exists by that node). By [def-weil-geometric-point] the pair consisting of the point $s$ and the field homomorphism $\iota:\kappa(s)\to\Omega$ is a morphism $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, a geometric point of $S$ lying over $s$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and a map $\kappa\to\Omega$, as [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] requires.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), statement ('let sbar be its closed point')

proof.text: *$\Gamma(S,-)$ is exact.* By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] (applied to $R$ strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $\bar s$ of step 1) the germ maps $\gamma_{\mathcal F}:\Gamma(S,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(S)\to\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ are isomorphisms of abelian groups, natural in $\mathcal F\in\Ab(S_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]: $\gamma$ is a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(S,-)\cong(-)_{\bar s}$ of functors $\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\textit{Ab}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] the stalk functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ is exact. Transfer along $\gamma$: (a) $\Gamma(S,-)$ is additive, since for morphisms $\varphi,\psi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ one has $(\varphi+\psi)_S=\varphi_S+\psi_S$ (morphisms of abelian sheaves are added sectionwise); (b) if $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal F''\to0$ is short exact in $\Ab(S_{\Et})$, then by naturality $\gamma_{\mathcal F}\circ a_S=a_{\bar s}\circ\gamma_{\mathcal F'}$ and $\gamma_{\mathcal F''}\circ b_S=b_{\bar s}\circ\gamma_{\mathcal F}$, so the sequence $0\to\mathcal F'(S)\to\mathcal F(S)\to\mathcal F''(S)\to0$ is carried by the isomorphisms $\gamma_{\mathcal F'},\gamma_{\mathcal F},\gamma_{\mathcal F''}$ onto the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'_{\bar s}\to\mathcal F_{\bar s}\to\mathcal F''_{\bar s}\to0$; kernels and images correspond under these isomorphisms, so it is short exact. Hence $\Gamma(S,-)$ is an additive functor carrying short exact sequences to short exact sequences, i.e. exact, and by the equivalence recorded in [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (Stacks Tag 010N) it commutes with finite limits and finite colimits. This is the first assertion of the statement.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), proof, first sentence ('If we show that Gamma(S,F) = F_sbar then Gamma(S,-) is exact as the stalk functor is exact')

proof.text: *Vanishing in positive degrees (the higher derived functors of an exact functor are zero, Stacks Derived Categories Lemma Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor) (5), whose proof is that an exact functor carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms; written out here for the definition of etale cohomology).* Let $\mathcal F\in\Ab(S_{\Et})$ and $p\ge1$. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(S,I^\bullet))$ where $\mathcal F\to I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], i.e. a quasi-isomorphism from the complex $\mathcal F[0]$ ($\mathcal F$ in degree $0$, zero elsewhere) to a K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves, and $\Gamma(S,I^\bullet)$ is the complex obtained by applying $\Gamma(S,-)$ termwise. A quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all cohomology objects [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $H^p(I^\bullet)\cong H^p(\mathcal F[0])$, and $H^p(\mathcal F[0])=\ker(0\to0)/\operatorname{im}(\mathcal F[0]^{p-1}\to0)=0$ because $\mathcal F[0]^p=0$ for $p\ne0$. By step 2, $\Gamma(S,-):\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\textit{Ab}$ is an additive functor between abelian categories [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] preserving finite limits and finite colimits, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives an isomorphism $H^p(\Gamma(S,I^\bullet))\cong\Gamma(S,H^p(I^\bullet))$. Since $H^p(I^\bullet)$ is a zero object and an additive functor carries zero objects to zero objects ($\mathrm{id}_0=0$ gives $\mathrm{id}_{\Gamma(S,0)}=\Gamma(S,0_{0,0})=0$), $\Gamma(S,H^p(I^\bullet))=0$. Hence $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p\ge1$.
